leaders.priorTitle: Chair of the graduate Bible and ministry department and director of the Doctor of Ministry program
leaders.priorInstitution: Abilene Christian University (internal promotion; ACU alumnus and faculty member since 1981)

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President
leaders.notes: Became ACU's 11th president June 1, 2010, after serving as the university's Executive Vice President; an ACU alumnus. No presidential search is publicly underway; he remains in office as of 2026.

leaders.notes: Marilyn and Stanley M. Katz Dean from 1984 to 2006; his 22-year tenure was a record for a U.S. medical school dean. He was a neuroscientist who had founded Einstein's neuroscience department.

leaders.priorTitle: Director of the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
leaders.notes: Marilyn and Stanley M. Katz Dean June 1, 2006 to June 30, 2018, and concurrently Vice President for Medical Affairs of Yeshiva University; recruited from a senior post at the NIH.

leaders.priorInstitution: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine

leaders.notes: Marilyn and Stanley M. Katz Dean July 16, 2018 to July 30, 2023; a cardiologist recruited from Johns Hopkins. His tenure spanned the deepening Montefiore Einstein integration.

leaders.priorTitle: Chair of the Department of Medicine at Einstein and Montefiore
leaders.priorInstitution: Albert Einstein College of Medicine / Montefiore (internal promotion; earlier at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai)
leaders.notes: Named the Marilyn and Stanley M. Katz Dean effective October 2, 2023 and Chief Academic Officer of Montefiore Einstein; the top leadership title is Dean (no separate president). His tenure follows Ruth L. Gottesman's landmark $1 billion gift (announced February 2024) making tuition free in perpetuity, amid Einstein's move toward independence from Yeshiva University.

leaders.notes: APU's 17th president, 2000-2019, and an alumnus who had served as Executive Vice President before his appointment; 19 years as president out of 43 years at APU.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: APU's 18th-numbered president (2019-2021); a toxicologist and former Ball State University president. He retired effective November 2021 after a short tenure.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Strategic Planning and Mission Integration

leaders.notes: Named interim president effective November 5, 2021, following Ferguson's retirement, serving until Adam Morris took office in July 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President, Chief Transformation Officer, and Chief Institutional Advancement Officer
leaders.notes: Became APU's 18th president July 1, 2022, recruited from senior executive roles at Biola University. Remains in office as of 2026.

leaders.notes: CGU's 15th president and first woman to lead the university, formally installed in fall 2010 (announced November 2010) and serving until 2015; a health economist and former Syracuse University provost.

leaders.priorTitle: University administrator/trustee
leaders.notes: Served as interim president after Freund's departure until stepping down effective December 31, 2016. Biographical detail is limited in official sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President and Provost

leaders.priorTitle: President
